subject.title: Synchronous crypto.createHash blocks Node.js event loop on large MCP schemas

question: Should this issue be treated as enough proof to queue a bundle-MCP config-hash performance fix, or should maintainers first ask for a focused reproduction that distinguishes large mcp.servers launch config from large returned tool schemas?
rationale: Source proves synchronous hashing on the prepare path, but the report's schema example does not feed the cited line and the best fix changes depending on which payload actually blocks Gateway heartbeats.

options.title: Ask For Focused Reproduction
options.body: Request a small repro or benchmark that separates large launch config from returned tool schemas before queueing automated repair.

options.title: Queue Config-Hash Repair
options.body: Treat the synchronous mergedConfig hash path as sufficient source proof and ask for a bounded nonblocking fingerprint helper plus regression coverage.

options.title: Split Schema Catalog Follow-Up
options.body: Keep this issue scoped to config hashing and open a separate item only if a returned-schema catalog repro is provided.

recommendation.title: Ask For Focused Reproduction
recommendation.body: Request a small repro or benchmark that separates large launch config from returned tool schemas before queueing automated repair.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and earlier CLI session hash history put this handle closest to the exact line and session-reuse invariant.
